title: oncall-handoff-notes-aisha-rahman
body:
Shift summary (02/27 -> 02/28):
- Night shift steady overall. Minor blips at ~03:10 UTC when p50 spiked from 45ms -> 220ms for ~8m. Root cause appears to be a single host in pool-nyc-gpu-3 with high CPU steal (suspect noisy neighbor / maintenance). Host removed from pool, autoscaler drained 2 pods, p50 returned to baseline.
- Deployments: rolling patch to model-v2.1 (quantization tweak) staged at 01:30 UTC, no immediate regressions but we saw increased 502s from a small subset (see incidents). Rollback ready (tag: model-v2.1-rollback) but not executed.

Open incidents / tasks:
1) 502 spike (02:18 - 02:24 UTC) - transient, ~0.4% of requests. Symptoms: immediate 502s with error paths indicating model load timeout (timeout=10s). Likely caused by concurrent model variant loads + warmup race. Action: monitor for recurrence, consider increasing model load timeout to 15s for this variant. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/210 (WIP).
2) Host CPU steal on pool-nyc-gpu-3 (03:10 UTC) - host taken OOD from pool; flagged host to infra team for host-level investigation. Follow-up: check provider maintenance / kernel updates. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-348.
3) Alert jitter: the p99 latency alert fired twice for a single region during the 03:10 event. Alerts seem noisy for brief spikes. Suggestion: switch p99 alert to sustained 3m window or add a mute rule for autoscaler-related transient events.

Temporary runbook snippets (draft) - goal: quick triage steps for common on-call events (keep short, link to full runbook in Confluence)
- High error rate (502/500) for hosted-api:
  1) Check status page / incidents dashboard (Console -> Observability -> Errors).
  2) Identify error patterns (are 502s tied to specific model, route, region?). Filter by model and region.
  3) If model load timeout: check model-serving logs on the instance (journalctl -u serving-runtime or container logs). Grep for 'model_load_timeout' and 'OOM' traces.
  4) If OOM suspected: confirm container OOM kills (kubectl describe pod) and check node memory pressure. If yes, scale down replica concurrency, enable fallback to quantized model.
  5) If it's a small fraction and appears to be warmup race: temporarily enable pre-warming for that model variant and consider increasing load timeout to 15s.
  6) If widespread and persistent: trigger canary rollback to previous model revision (tag: stable) and inform product/ML.

- Increased latency (p50/p90/p99 spikes):
  1) Check autoscaling events (Console -> Dedicated -> Pool -> Events) for recent scale or drain.
  2) Check for single-host issues (kubectl get pods -o wide, check node CPU/memory).
  3) Look for KV cache misses - correlate with cache-miss metric (cache.kv.miss.rate). If miss rate spikes, it explains higher latency.
  4) If noisy neighbor suspected: cordon node, evict heavy pods, and let autoscaler replace.

Quick commands/places to check:
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=serving-runtime --tail=200
- kubectl -n serving describe pod <pod-name>
- ssh to host (only if infra advises) -> sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 500
- Console -> Observability -> Dashboards -> Serving Runtime Latency / Errors

Escalation & contact list:
- Primary SRE on-call: Noah Thompson (slack: @noah, phone: pager)
- Secondary: Jordan Lee (slack: @jordlee)
- Infra lead (for host issues): Priya Menon (slack: @priya)
notes_to_self:
- Remember to follow up with infra team about host kernel updates (INFRA-348).
- Add a short-lived Grafana panel for model-load-time distribution (p95/p99) to detect warmup races.
- Draft PR to increase model load timeout for edge-case variants (start from PR 210).
- Revisit alert thresholds for p99 latency (discuss with SRE on next weekly).
- Consider adding a 'warmup' flag to deployment pipeline for heavy models to reduce race conditions.

Rough TODO (prioritized):
1) Finish PR to increase model load timeout + tests (Aisha).
2) Add Grafana panel for model load times (Noah).
3) Write a short post-mortem if 502s repeat (owner: Aisha).
4) Follow up with infra on host CPU steal (Jordan -> INFRA-348).

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Did provider (cloud region) run maintenance in the window? Check provider incident page and infra ticket notes.
- Is the quantized-variant rollout correlated with the 502s? Need A/B logs by user-agent/model-variant.
- Are autoscaler drain events causing transient p99 spikes? If so, can we add a 30s grace window to p99 alerting?

Other notes (freeform / scratch):
- Short-term mitigation for warmup race: set model warmup to 2 replicas on deploy for heavy models (manual toggle in deployment YAML).
- If this becomes frequent, propose an orchestration change: prefer asynchronous model loading with soft-fail + fallback variant to keep requests serving.
- Link to existing full runbook (do not duplicate): CONFLUENCE-ENG/Runbooks/serving-runtime-kv-cache

End of handoff. Night shift, signing off—Aisha.
